newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ANZ hires consultant to boost defences.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ANZ hires consultant to boost defences.

text.p: The Australia and New Zealand Banking Group (ANZ) said on Thursday it had hired a U.S. management consultant to comb the group for efficiencies as part of the bank's strategy to shore up defences against takeover.

ANZ, seen as vulnerable to takeover if Australia's freeze on big-bank mergers is lifted this year, said it has engaged KPMG Barents to help accelerate and broaden efficiencies across the group. It said it had set up a steering committee chaired by the bank's chief executive, Don Mercer, to oversee the process.

"The next stage of our transformation programme is to look at how we can leverage improvements we make in one part of ANZ so that we can apply them in other parts of the group," Mercer said in an internal bank memo released to Reuters on Thursday.

"This will allow is to truly gain advantage from our size and scale, wil remove geographic orientations in how we view and solve problems and allow us to take advantage of the efficiencies that come from operating on a global basis."
ANZ made the memo available after parts of it were quoted in a local newspaper report on Thursday.
"To help us we have engaged international management consultants KPMG Barents who will provide both strategic and logistical support," the bank added.
The memo did not mention the threat of takeover directly, but a spokeswoman told Reuters that "that's one part of it".
Mercer has cited good performance and a strong share price as the best defences against takeover, but ANZ's cost-to-income ratio is the weakest of the four big banks at 67.3 percent.
"It's all part of making the bank more competitive," the spokeswoman added.

The federal government's Wallis inquiry into the financial system is expected to recommend the loosening of regulations which currently limit mergers and takeovers involving major Australian banks and life offices when it reports in March.
